In 2024, the United States continued to experience economic growth while also continuing to experience persistent inflation in excess of the U.S. Federal Reserve Board’s target rate.
The U.S. Federal Reserve Board lowered the target range for the federal funds rate three times in 2024, including a rate reduction in December lowering the target range to 4.25-4.50%.
GDP growth in the Eurozone in 2024 was moderately positive.

In Europe, the European Central Bank lowered rates four times in 2024, lowering the deposit

rate to 3% as Eurozone inflation slowed as compared to the prior year albeit remaining above the European Central Bank’s 2% inflation target.
The Bank of Japan raised interest rates twice in 2024, ultimately up to 0.25%.
In China, the economy grew in 2024, but Chinese growth remains subject to various headwinds including in the property sector.
